bridge: Builds on I02 injection, W11 object access and P04 data provenance.
teaching:
Retrieval-augmented generation selects external information and places it into a model context. Indexing creates chunks and representations; retrieval chooses candidates; generation uses them. Every stage needs tenant/owner context. An access check after generation is too late if private text already reached an unauthorised context or provider.

Similarity search ranks relevance, not permission. Filter by effective ACL before exposure, carry provenance and recheck policy as documents change. Shared caches must include the relevant identity/policy context. Deleting a source can also require deleting derived chunks, cached responses and memory entries under the retention policy.

Retrieved content may be wrong, stale or instruction-bearing. Citations help locate evidence but do not prove it is true or that the answer follows from it. Validate output handling separately and show uncertainty when permitted sources do not support an answer. The supplied fixture uses a plain list rather than installing a vector database.

The assigned Microsoft video is a worked example of pre-generation document filtering, not a requirement to deploy Azure. An embedding is a numerical representation used to compare content; semantic proximity expresses relevance under that representation, not permission, truth or ownership. In this exercise, ownership and explicit public status are authoritative policy fields. Missing or malformed access metadata must be denied or quarantined, not treated as public by default.

Authentication and retrieval permission are separate checks. Decoding a token’s JSON does not validate it: a deployed system must validate its signature, issuer, intended audience, expiry and accepted tenant, then derive permitted scope from trusted server-side state. Use the tenant together with its user/object identifier; do not trust a caller-supplied user ID or an arbitrary group list. A valid identity does not grant every indexed document. Revocation has to reach the document, all derived chunks and any cached answers or group membership used for decisions; define the actual freshness bound rather than promising immediate revocation from one index update.
example:
Documents
D1 owner=A text="meeting Monday" score 0.80
D2 owner=B text="private salary" score 0.99
D3 public  text="office hours 9-5" score 0.70
Caller A; allowed scope=own + public.
Correct pre-context candidates: D1,D3.
Incorrect: choose highest score D2, then redact after generation.
explanation: D2's high relevance does not authorise its disclosure. The failure occurs when its content crosses the retrieval boundary, even if the eventual answer omits the salary. Preserve document ID/version and ACL decision without writing private body text into shared debug logs.
exercise: Rank permitted documents for A and B under own+public. Then add an explicit policy rule: archived documents are unavailable to ordinary retrieval, including their owner, and D1 is now archived. State which retrieval/index/cache decisions must change for A. Explain one way a citation can exist while a generated claim is unsupported.
solution: Initially A receives D1 then D3 by score; B receives D2 then D3. After the explicit archived rule applies to D1, A receives only D3; ownership no longer suffices for an archived document. Block stale D1 chunks/context and cached answers under the actual freshness/invalidation contract. A citation may point to a passage that does not support the statement. An archive flag in one database does not prove all derived copies are immediately removed.
challenge: Design a tenant-aware retrieval cache key and a negative test where A/B ask the same question. Include document-policy version changes and explain why caching only by query text is unsafe.
challenge_solution: Include authenticated scope/tenant and relevant policy/document versions or use a design that reauthorises results on every read. Same query text must not reuse another user's private context or answer. Define invalidation/retention explicitly.
